# Benny

> Benny, the always-on coding agent for GitHub issues. An open-source Devin alternative: mention it in an issue, agree the requirements, and it opens a pull request. It runs on your own Cloudflare account with your Claude Code or OpenCode Go subscription. MIT licence.

Every issue gets its own agent, which keeps its context and its work branch and sleeps between comments. Benny opens pull requests and cannot merge, approve or close one; a person always merges.

## Pages

- [Benny](https://benny.heyshoo.in/): what it is, how one request goes from mention to pull request, and how it compares with Devin, Capy and Factory's Droids.
- [Software factory](https://benny.heyshoo.in/software-factory/): issues go in, reviewed pull requests come out, with schedules for repeating work.
- [For teams](https://benny.heyshoo.in/for-teams/): a self-hosted AI software engineer set up on your team's own accounts.
- [Blog](https://benny.heyshoo.in/blog/): notes on running a software factory on GitHub; RSS at https://benny.heyshoo.in/rss.xml.
  - [I don't want to learn another agentic UI](https://benny.heyshoo.in/blog/i-dont-want-another-agentic-ui.md): why I run my software factory on GitHub with a self-hosted coding agent, and what it costs (Markdown).

## Project

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/madscientist111/benny): the source, MIT licensed.
- [README](https://github.com/madscientist111/benny#readme): why it was built, how it is built, what it may and may not do, and its limitations.

## Background

- [Building always-on agents](https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-always-on-agents): Anthropic's article on agents that sleep between events; Benny works this way.
